REVISEThe main all-size mathematical results survive review, but the note contains a false assertion about the bridge matching. The correction preserves all the displayed stacked-receiver formulas. The normalization theorem, same-P two-gap lemma, transition bound, complete  $8\times4$  example, explicit cooperative repair, and earlier tile-cycle inequality  $d\le \nu_R$  have valid written arguments under the conventions detailed below.The most consequential bookkeeping clarification is that the witness graph used in
$$2\rho(R)=-2L+\sigma+c-d-p-u$$
must have exactly the  $k$  internally attached saturated owners as its vertices. Using all  $Q=k+\eta$  saturated endpoints instead changes that identity.This is a review of the supplied mathematical text. The reported executions, declaration counts, earlier review outcomes, and Lean results are not verification evidence used in this verdict.1. Required correction: the bridge’s matching description is falseIn New Note §4, the sentence“Its P is matched inside the two-tile bridge.”is false for the listed matching.For the bridge between blocks  $i$  and  $i+1$ , write
$$H_i=(4i+3,1),\qquad B_{i+1}=(4i+4,1).$$
The actual matching incidences are:Endpoint in a bridge tileIts matching mateMate’s location $(8i+6,2)\in H_i$  $(8i+6,1)$ Omitted deficient tile  $(4i+3,0)$  $(8i+6,3)\in H_i$  $(8i+5,3)$ Included central deficient tile  $(4i+2,1)$  $(8i+9,2)\in B_{i+1}$  $(8i+9,1)$ Omitted deficient tile  $(4i+4,0)$ Thus the second bridge tile’s unique  $P$  is matched outside  $R_r$ . There is no matching edge between the two bridge tiles.The reason that the bridge introduces no saturated attachment is that all three listed mates lie in deficient tiles. Their membership in the receiver is a separate question.A concrete replacement paragraph is:Each first bridge tile has  $t=1,b=1$  and charge zero; each second bridge tile has  $t=1,b=2$  and charge  $-1/2$ . Every matching endpoint in these tiles has its mate in a deficient tile, so the bridge pair introduces no saturated attachment. Adding the first bridge tile internalizes one former receiver-boundary crossing and introduces one new deficient-to-deficient crossing. Adding the second bridge tile introduces another deficient-to-deficient crossing. Consequently each bridge pair increases  $j$  by exactly one.This also corrects the later phrase “the added crossing.” There are two newly introduced boundary crossings and one removed boundary crossing, giving a net increase of one. The claimed value
$$j=2r+(r-1)=3r-1$$
is correct.2. Exact charge and owner conventionsThe supplied attachment ledger is consistent, including its boundary signs.A saturated tile with a matching endpoint has diagonal selected corners and one  $P$ . Its mate cannot be in the same tile, and cannot be in another saturated tile: a matching edge between saturated tiles would create adjacent companion  $T$  vertices across the shared face, each already adjacent to its own internal  $P$ .Consequently
$$Q=k+\eta.$$
Summing the deficient-tile charge formula gives
$$2\rho(R)
=\sum_{\text{deficient }U\subset R}(t_U-b_U+s_U)
=-D+k+\sigma.$$
In particular,  $\eta$  does not enter this sum as another attachment debt.For the parity identity, if  $\mu_R$  counts physical matching edges wholly inside  $R$ , then
$$4|R|=t+b+2\mu_R+j,
\qquad
D=b-t+Q.$$
Hence
$$D\equiv j+Q\pmod 2.$$
These arguments apply to disconnected regions as well as connected ones.The witness ledger needs an explicit definitionFor the diagonal-witness identity
$$2\rho(R)=-2L+\sigma+c-d-p-u,
\tag{W}$$
state the following conventions where the identity is invoked:The owner set  $\mathcal A$  consists of saturated tiles in  $R$  whose  $P$  is matched to a deficient tile in  $R$ . Thus
$$|\mathcal A|=k.$$
Reserve one internal blank for each deficient selected vertex, and two additional distinct blanks for each marked tile. These reservations are disjoint. $F$  contains all remaining deficient blanks, including blanks with no adjacent owner. Thus
$$|F|=D-2L.$$
With these conventions,
$$|F|=e+p+u,\qquad e=k-c+d,$$
so
$$c-d-p-u=k-|F|,$$
which proves (W).If  $H$  instead includes all  $Q$  saturated owners in  $R$ , including those counted by  $\eta$ , the correct formula is
$$2\rho(R)=-2L+\sigma-\eta+c-d-p-u.
\tag{W'}$$
This distinction does not change the new examples, where  $\eta=0$ , but matters for a general boundary-crossing theorem. If the preceding blank-witness note already fixes  $|\mathcal A|=k$ , this is a clarification to repeat, rather than a mathematical change.All regional sums must use charges assigned by one fixed full configuration. After a promotion, reconstruct the charges and witness objects before applying another ledger.3. Bundle, single, cycle, and normalization assertionsThese assertions are valid.Bundle lemmaFor the selected matching edges, matching disjointness makes  $T,X,Y$  pairwise disjoint, and the surviving matching avoids  $T\cup X$ . Its occupied set is exactly
$$A'=(T\cup X)\cup V(M')=A\setminus Y.$$
Every old selected vertex therefore remains feasible. The only new selected-vertex conditions are precisely
$$\deg_{A'}(x)\le 1\quad(x\in X).$$
This proves both directions of the stated equivalence.The objective calculation is exact:
$$|T\cup X|+|M'|
=(|T|+|X|)+(|M|-|X|)
=|T|+|M|.$$
Single and cycle promotionsFor a single promotion, the removed mate is an occupied neighbor, so an endpoint of occupied degree at most two has remaining occupied degree at most one.For a directed cycle, each promoted  $x_i$  loses two distinct occupied neighbors: its own mate and the next candidate’s mate. Initial occupied degree three therefore suffices. Matching disjointness ensures that all physical vertices used by this alternating cycle are distinct. The interpretation as an  $M$ -alternating even cycle is correct; a two-node dependency cycle in the square grid is a square.Termination and maximalityEvery allowed move removes at least one matching edge and retains all previously selected vertices. Recomputing the current conditions after each move gives termination after at most  $|M_0|$  moves.At termination:no matching endpoint has occupied degree at most two;neither current degree-three dependency digraph contains a directed cycle.That is exactly the claimed normal form. An objective maximizer with maximal  $|T|$  cannot admit one of these promotions, since it would preserve the objective and increase  $|T|$ .There is no need for confluence, and none has been proved.Two minor precision edits are appropriate:Specify finite simple undirected graphs, or define occupied degree explicitly as the number of distinct occupied neighbors.For a uniform runtime statement including the empty-matching case and the initial examination, write
$$O\!\left((|M_0|+1)(|V|+|E|)\right).$$
The printed bound is equivalent for nonempty matchings. Linear storage and a quadratic upper bound on bounded-degree grids are correct.4. Same-P two-gap lemma and transition boundThe two-gap proof is sufficient and handles matching edges crossing the receiver boundary.Northwest intervening tileFor common BR  $P$ -state, the owners’ selected vertices already have their internal occupied  $P$  neighbor. This forces the intervening tile’s BR corner blank. The relevant external neighbors of its TR and BL corners are the owners’ blank TL corners.If this deficient tile had  $b=t$ , the forced blank and  $t\le1$  imply
$$b=t=1.$$
Its other three corners contain one  $T$  and two  $P$ 's. $T$  at TL has two occupied internal neighbors. $T$  at TR leaves a  $P$  at BL with one occupied internal neighbor, a forced external blank below, and at most one occupied external neighbor to the left. $T$  at BL gives the symmetric contradiction.In the latter two cases the offending  $P$  has full occupied degree at most two. Its mate cannot evade the argument by crossing  $R$ : every possible mate is already among the physical neighbors being counted. A missing outer-boundary neighbor only decreases the degree.Southeast intervening tileIts TL corner is forced blank, while the relevant external neighbors of TR and BL are occupied owner  $P$ 's.Again  $b=t=1$  would give: $T$  at BR with two occupied internal neighbors; or $T$  at TR or BL with an occupied internal neighbor and an occupied external neighbor.All cases violate feasibility. Rotation by  $180^\circ$  supplies the common-TL case.Thus both deficient tiles have gap at least one for every equal-state link.Disjointness and boundary termsThe owners have coordinate sum  $r_0+c_0$ . The two intermediate families have sums  $r_0+c_0-1$  and  $r_0+c_0+1$ , and row coordinates distinguish links within either family. Therefore all counted intermediate tiles are distinct, and
$$D\ge 2(v-1-a)$$
uses no tile twice.There are exactly  $v$  saturated matching endpoints in  $R$ , so
$$Q=v=k+\eta.$$
Substitution gives
$$\begin{aligned}
2\rho(R)
&=-D+k+\sigma\\
&\le -2(v-1-a)+v-\eta+\sigma\\
&=2-v+2a+\sigma-\eta.
\end{aligned}$$
The signs of both crossing terms are correct.For a homogeneous chain,  $v\ge4$  and  $\sigma\le\eta$  indeed imply  $\rho(R)\le-1$ .State the source packing preciselyThe compensation conclusion is valid provided each receiver is disjoint from its assigned sources and the combined receiver-plus-source regions are pairwise tile-disjoint. Each source allowance must be used once, and the remaining tiles must have nonpositive original charge.Pairwise disjoint sources alone would not suffice if they overlapped their receivers. Where the final grid inequality is inferred from a tile partition, the board must be covered by those tiles, or any uncovered boundary strip must be separately accounted for.The normalization theorem supplies none of these packing or boundary-imbalance hypotheses.5. The complete  $8\times4$  example is correctThe six listed edges are grid edges with pairwise disjoint endpoints, and none meets  $T$ . Every selected vertex has exactly one occupied neighbor.The occupied degrees of all twelve matching endpoints are:Vertex rowColumns containing  $P$ Occupied degrees in that order $1$  $0,1,2$  $3,3,3$  $2$  $0,1,2$  $3,3,4$  $5$  $1,2,3$  $4,3,3$  $6$  $1,2,3$  $3,3,3$ Thus the pair is single-promotion-terminal, with precisely the two stated degree-four owner endpoints.The complete original tile-charge accounting is:Tile $t$  $b$  $p$  $\rho_Q$  $(0,0)$ 112 $0$  $(0,1)$ 121 $-1/2$  $(1,0)$ 112 $1/2$  $(1,1)$ 211 $0$  $(2,0)$ 211 $0$  $(2,1)$ 112 $1/2$  $(3,0)$ 121 $-1/2$  $(3,1)$ 112 $0$ Each positively charged deficient tile has one matching attachment to a saturated owner. The other deficient tiles have none.For the central region, the only matching boundary crossings are
$$(2,0)-(1,0),\qquad (5,3)-(6,3).$$
Both are deficient-to-deficient. Therefore
$$D=0,\quad k=Q=2,\quad \sigma=\eta=0,\quad j=2,\quad \rho(R)=1.$$
The deficient tiles’ sole blanks,  $(3,1)$  and  $(4,2)$ , are necessarily reserved for their selected vertices. Hence  $F=\varnothing$ , and the witness graph has two isolated owners.The full grid has
$$|T|+|M|=10+6=16,$$
and charge zero. Its exterior has charge  $-1$ .This establishes the claimed false candidate rule: occupied degree at least three at every matching endpoint does not force regional nonpositivity, even with  $\sigma=\eta=0$ .It also establishes sharpness of the coefficient  $2$  on  $a$  in the stated degree-only transition theorem:
$$v=2,\quad a=1,\quad \sigma=\eta=0,\quad 2\rho(R)=2.$$
It does not establish sharpness after imposing the stronger acyclic normal form, since this example contains the displayed dependency cycles.6. All stacked receiver formulas hold after the bridge correctionAt each block interface, the two facing rows have occupied vertices in opposite column parities. Thus stacking creates no occupied adjacency. Feasibility and all occupied degrees are unchanged, for every  $r\ge1$ .The  $r$  central squares contribute  $4r$  tiles. The bridges contribute  $2(r-1)$  distinct tiles and connect successive squares through column one. Hence
$$|R_r|=6r-2,$$
and  $R_r$  is tile-connected.Each bridge pair contributes: $1$  to  $D$ ;zero to  $k,Q,\sigma,\eta$ ;a net increase of  $1$  to  $j$ .Consequently
$$D=r-1,\qquad k=Q=2r,\qquad \sigma=\eta=0,$$

$$j=3r-1,\qquad
2\rho(R_r)=-(r-1)+2r=r+1.$$
These are general counting arguments, independent of a finite range of controls.The complementary charge can also be checked directly. The omitted tiles are the top-left and bottom-left tile of each block, the first block’s top-right tile, and the last block’s bottom-right tile. Their charges sum to
$$0-\frac r2-\frac12+0=-\frac{r+1}{2}.$$
The private-blank count is exactThere are no marked caps here, so  $L=0$ .Every deficient central tile and every first bridge tile has a unique blank, which is reserved. For a second bridge tile  $B_q=(4q,1)$ ,  $1\le q\le r-1$ :its selected vertex is  $(8q,2)$ ;its unique internal blank neighbor is  $(8q,3)$ , which must be reserved;its remaining blank is
$$z_q=(8q+1,3).$$
The blank  $z_q$  is adjacent to exactly one owner, through the selected corner  $(8q+2,3)$ . Its other neighbors are a blank, a  $P$ , and the absent right-hand boundary neighbor.Thus the entire free set consists of these  $r-1$  distinct private blanks:
$$c=2r,\qquad p=r-1,\qquad d=u=0.$$
There is no repeated allocation, and the witness ledger gives
$$2\rho=2r-(r-1)=r+1.$$
The all- $r$  family therefore proves unbounded positive charge on tile-connected, single-promotion-terminal receivers.7. The cooperative repair is valid for every  $r$ For the upper two-cycle, take
$$X=\{(2,1),(1,2)\},\qquad
Y=\{(2,2),(1,1)\}.$$
Both promoted vertices initially have occupied degree three and are adjacent to both deleted vertices. After the bundle move: $(2,1)$  has only the occupied neighbor  $(2,0)$ ; $(1,2)$  has only the occupied neighbor  $(0,2)$ .The remaining endpoint  $(1,0)$  then has occupied neighbors exactly
$$(0,0),\ (2,0).$$
Promoting it singly and deleting its mate  $(2,0)$  is legal.The specified lower moves are exactly the image under
$$(r,c)\longmapsto(7-r,3-c),$$
which preserves the original block configuration. They are therefore valid by the same argument.Each block loses all six matching edges, gains six selected vertices, retains its original ten selected vertices, and preserves its objective. The changed rows are  $1,2,5,6$ , so different blocks do not interfere.The final configuration has
$$M=\varnothing,\qquad |T|=16r.$$
More explicitly, every aligned tile has exactly two selected vertices after the repair. Every reconstructed tile charge is therefore zero, including every tile of the former positive receiver.Two wording changes would improve precision:Replace “strictly inside a block” by “no move crosses a block interface; the facing boundary rows are unchanged.” Some promoted vertices lie in boundary columns  $0$  and  $3$ .Say “the displayed cooperative normalization sequence eliminates this family.” The proof establishes this sequence; it does not establish an order-independent outcome for every normalization sequence.The original regional ledger and the reconstructed final ledger are separate applications. Their charge resources must not be added together.8. The earlier tile-cycle bound  $d\le\nu_R$  is validThe proof in Diagonal and Tile-Cycle Background §4 is sufficient for every finite region of the ordinary square grid.A double link between consecutive owners consists of two distinct physical free blanks. They lie in the two different intermediate deficient tiles between the diagonal owner tiles. All four tiles belong to  $R$ , so they form a unit-square cycle in  $G_R$ .The map from double links to squares is injective. A second owner pair cannot use the other diagonal of the same square: those two tiles are deficient, whereas owner tiles are saturated.Distinctness alone would not prove the cycle-rank bound, but the supplied independence argument does. In any nonempty collection of these unit squares, select one with minimal top-row coordinate. Its upper edge could belong to another unit square only immediately above it. No such square is selected. The symmetric difference of the chosen boundaries is therefore nonempty.Their cycle vectors are consequently linearly independent over  $\mathbb F_2$ . Restriction to the nonforest edges of a spanning forest is injective on the cycle space, and there are
$$|E(G_R)|-|R|+\operatorname{components}(G_R)=\nu_R$$
such edges. Hence
$$d\le\nu_R.$$
This proves the bound without finite enumeration. Disconnected regions and missing outer-boundary neighbors cause no exception.Payment interpretationThe bound gives a necessary structural limit on double links. It does not assert that each tile cycle supplies a free double link. The mixed diamond itself has a tile-adjacency cycle and no free shared blank.The three quantities must retain separate meanings:a double link contributes its actual free blanks to the witness ledger;its unit-square cycle certifies the structural bound  $d\le\nu_R$ ;a dependency cycle authorizes a promotion that changes the configuration.The same double link does not receive an additional charge credit merely because its tile cycle has been identified.For a tile forest,  $d=0$ , so the stated forest formula follows. The condition
$$p+u\ge c+\sigma$$
is exact for the worst-case source allowance  $L$  under this ledger. For actual source charge  $s<L$ , the supplied correction
$$\rho(R\cup\text{sources})
=\frac{\sigma+c-d-p-u}{2}-(L-s)$$
correctly retains the unused allowance. Failure of the worst-case certificate does not prove positive actual union charge.The separate all-subset staircase sharpness construction refers to an earlier matching list absent from this input. Its geometric increments and  $\nu_{R_I}=|I|$  argument are consistent, conditional on that base construction. If that full physical fixture is to be covered by a standalone review, include its original matching definition. The general tile-cycle bound does not depend on that omitted fixture.Required dispositionRevise the false bridge-mate sentence and its crossing explanation. State the internal-owner and complete-reservation conventions explicitly, and make the receiver/source partition requirement precise. The graph convention, empty-matching runtime bound, and wording about the exhibited normalization sequence need the minor edits described above.With those changes, the listed written all-size results are acceptable. The examples refute the proposed regional rules under single-promotion terminality; they leave the unrestricted grid inequality and compensation in the stronger acyclic normal form unresolved. No conclusion here claims that the full note is Lean-formalized.
